incidents.summary: New drought impacts and responses reported for early October 2026. In the US, Lebanon County, Pennsylvania returned to normal drought status and lifted water conservation requests, while Baltimore, Maryland faced 20-year low reservoir levels and began drawing from the Susquehanna River. Drought damage to crops in North Carolina reduced yields for corn, tobacco, and peanuts. Internationally, Sri Lanka faces severe drought with empty wells, South West Water in the UK received a drought permit to support supplies, and Karnataka, India released ₹1,250 crore in drought relief as rice prices spike due to production losses.

A severe drought is affecting multiple regions globally as of late July 2026. In Europe, an "exceptionally serious" drought has hit half of England and all of Wales, while the Rhine River dropped to its lowest ever level in the Netherlands and the Danube reached record lows in Budapest, disrupting tourism and industry. In the United States, drought conditions worsened in states like Minnesota and Michigan, while other areas like the Grand Strand in South Carolina are lifting drought management plans, and parts of Virginia and North Carolina are seeing improvements.
New drought developments include worsening conditions in Maine and Minnesota, with 35% of Minnesota in severe drought, while South Carolina's Lowcountry remains under extreme drought despite summer storms. In Europe, record-low river levels continue to disrupt power output and transport, and wildfire risk is elevated across the continent. Jamaica faces a potential $500 million drought response, and drone footage highlights the drought's impact in England.

The river, which flows through 10 countries, has receded to unprecedented lows, exposing rocks and old shipwrecks. In Budapest, the Danube was measured at just 23 centimeters, breaking previous records. River cruise ships are docking upriver, and sightseeing cruises have been canceled. A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia's Flores region near Ende on August 14, 2026, toppling buildings and killing at least two people. The shallow quake triggered a tsunami warning for four provinces, prompting mass evacuations before the alert was later lifted. Several strong aftershocks were reported.
The death toll from the magnitude 7.7 earthquake near Ende, Indonesia has risen to at least 38, with dozens injured and many buildings collapsed or damaged. Rescuers are searching for survivors in affected areas, and tsunami waves of less than 1 meter were recorded in several locations before the warning was lifted.

news.body: JAKARTA (Reuters) — An earthquake of magnitude 7.7 and several aftershocks struck off the coast of eastern Indonesia early on Saturday, the nation’s geophysics agency BMKG said, while tsunami waves of less than 1 metre (3 feet) were recorded in several areas. Many rushed from their homes, but there were no initial reports of damage from the quake, which was felt strongly for around one minute in regions such as Nagekeo and Bima, said Dodi Yuleova, the spokesperson for the national disaster mitigation agency. A video on Facebook, verified by Reuters as located at a port in Maumere, the main town in Sikka Regency on Flores Island in eastern Indonesia, showed parts of a building collapsing in dust and rubble as people screamed and ran in the street. A hospital in the district of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara Province was moving patients outside, Kompas TV footage showed. BMKG recorded the first quake at 4:58 a.m. (2158 GMT) at a depth of 15 km (9 miles), followed by several aftershocks.

incidents.summary: A strong earthquake struck Vanuatu on October 8, 2026, with the U.S. Geological Survey reporting a magnitude of 6.6 (later also cited as 6.3 by other sources) and a shallow depth of 10 km. The epicenter was located about 105–110 km northeast of Norsup (or east of Luganville) in the Penama region. Several news outlets confirmed the event, though slight variations in reported magnitude appeared.
